item.title: Georgia man, 18, charged with murder after dismembered human remains found in car trunk
item.description: Kingston Lammar Bradley, 18, faces murder charges after witnesses found human remains in a container near his Smyrna, Georgia, apartment complex.
item.content:encoded:
Police in Georgia charged 18-year-old Kingston Lammar Bradley with malice murder Friday after allegedly discovering trash bags filled with dismembered remains in the trunk of his car.

Witnesses spotted Bradley walking in his apartment complex with a container, and when he realized he was seen, he dropped the container and ran into his apartment, Smyrna Police Lt. Meredith Holt said during a news conference Friday.

Witnesses called the police after finding human remains inside the container, Holt said.

GEORGIA PAIR CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER BARTENDER'S DISMEMBERED REMAINS FOUND IN LAKE OUTSIDE ATLANTA

Police had previously responded to his home after a missing woman’s family reported her car and phone were at the location, Holt said, but they did not execute a search warrant.

After the witnesses found the human remains, police returned with a search warrant for Bradley’s car and found a garbage bag pulled tightly, "showing the outline of a body part," according to a news release from the department.

SINGER D4VD PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO MURDER OF YOUNG GIRL ALLEGEDLY FOUND DISMEMBERED, DECOMPOSING IN HIS CAR

Police called the Cobb County Medical Examiner’s office, which confirmed the bags contained human remains.

Smyrna Police Chief Keith Zgonc identified the victim as Shanteria "KT" Mosley, whose family reported her missing.

IF YOU'RE KNOCKING OUT DOORDASH DRIVERS WITH A BASEBALL BAT AFTER THEY HONK AT YOU, POLICE WOULD LIKE A WORD

Holt confirmed Mosley was a DoorDash worker, noting the company told police she had not been working on the day she went missing, according to a report from affiliate FOX 5 Atlanta.

DoorDash told People Magazine her account was last active on Tuesday.

Police do not yet know what connection Bradley had to the victim, Holt said.

"This is a shocking crime, I don’t know how else to describe it. I’ve been in law enforcement for 25 years and I have been a part of multiple homicide cases and I’ve worked crimes against children for 16 years, and this is a particularly gruesome crime," Holt said during the news conference.

"I cannot imagine what the family is going through," she added.

PHILADELPHIA HOME LINKED TO 7 MISSING WOMEN, LATE RESIDENT'S POTENTIAL 'SERIAL KILLER' MEMOIR INVESTIGATED

Police are still actively looking for other human remains, Holt said.

Bradley is facing additional charges for concealing the death of a person.

SINGER D4VD SHOWS NO EMOTION AS DETECTIVE RECOUNTS GRUESOME DISCOVERY OF TEEN'S DISMEMBERED REMAINS: REPORT

Holt said police had been called to Bradley's apartment multiple times in the past for domestic disputes, but said nothing indicated he was capable of a murder of this nature.

Bradley appeared in Cobb County Magistrate Court on Thursday, where a judge denied him bond, according to FOX 5. His next court hearing is scheduled for October.

Fox News Digital contacted the Smyrna Police Department and DoorDash for further comment.

item.title: Lauren Sánchez Bezos sparks backlash with ‘inappropriate’ plunging dress at state dinner
item.description: Lauren Sánchez Bezos sparked fierce debate over her plunging black dress at the White House state dinner honoring Chinese President Xi Jinping.
item.content:encoded:
Lauren Sánchez Bezos sent the internet buzzing when she arrived to a state dinner at the White House.

The 56-year-old former journalist attended the dinner with her husband, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, in honor of Chinese President Xi Jinping, in a figure-hugging black off-the-shoulder dress with a plunging neckline.

She paired the look with diamond drop earrings and a large statement diamond necklace.

Many X users took issue with Lauren's choice, calling her out for showing too much cleavage at such a high-profile event, with some even questioning why they were even there.

LAUREN SÁNCHEZ BEZOS HEATS UP AHEAD OF MET GALA WITH STRING OF DARING, SKIN-BARING LOOKS

"Money does not buy one class. She dresses terribly. So inappropriate." one user wrote.

"Why are they invited to an event and eating on the tax payer dime?" one user asked, while another wrote, "Have some dignity for goodness sake. This is a state dinner and you are 56 years old."

There were others who came to her defense online, writing that it isn't anyone's business what she chooses to wear and that they thought she looked nice.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Who else doesn't care and thinks she should wear whatever she wants?!!!" one user asked. Another added, "She looks great, and Jeff is very lucky to be her husband."

"She’s come a long way from being the entertainment reporter on the local LA news station," a third wrote. "Good for her."

This is not the first time Lauren has caused controversy with one of her outfits, as she also received criticism for the outfit she wore to President Trump's inauguration in January 2025.

She wore a white Alexander McQueen pantsuit featuring a fitted satin-trimmed blazer with a dangerously low-cut V-neck with her risqué white lace bustier popping out from underneath.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"Good grief, Lauren Sanchez. Put them away for one day," one user wrote at the time, while another added, "Really, a bra plainly visible. Today is NOT a night club event. Show some class & dignity."

item.title: Trump claims stunning casualty numbers in Russia-Ukraine war
item.description: Trump claims 25,000 people died last month in the Ukraine-Russia war and reveals he pushed Volodomyr Zelenskyy to settle with Vladimir Putin.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump said Saturday that 25,000 people were killed last month and another 32,000 the month before in the war between Ukraine and Russia

"Last month, 25,000 people died in the Ukraine-Russia war, okay? 25,000," he told reporters on the White House lawn Saturday.

"The month before that, 32,000 people died … mostly soldiers, 97% soldiers. But whether they're soldiers or civilians, think of it: 32,000. Two months ago, 33,000 people; this month, 25,000 people died. What a shame," he added.

PUTIN UNLEASHES NEW FURY ON UKRAINE AS REPORT EXPOSES FEAR HANGING OVER WAR’S END

Russia alone has lost as many as 450,000 soldiers since invading Ukraine in 2022, according to the Center for Strategic & International Studies (CSIS).

Trump also told reporters he wants to see an end to the war soon, revealing he spoke to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy recently.

KUSHNER, WITKOFF SET FOR KYIV TALKS AFTER PUTIN MEETING IN US PUSH FOR PEACE

"I spoke to him a lot, and he's going along and Putin's going along. And someday, hopefully in the not too distant future, maybe before the heavy winter, they'll make a deal," he told reporters.

He claimed that he pushed Zelenskyy to try to make a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

TRUMP NEGOTIATORS WITKOFF, KUSHNER MEET WITH PUTIN IN MOSCOW AS US PUSHES FOR END TO RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR

"I agreed with Zelenskyy that we talked about a lot of different subjects, and many of those subjects, very strong agreement. But you know what I want him to do? Make a deal. I want him to settle with Putin, and I want Putin to settle with him.

Zelenskyy announced Friday that Trump had agreed to give approval to Ukraine to license and produce U.S. Patriot missile interceptors.

TRUMP SAYS US WILL LET UKRAINE MAKE PATRIOT MISSILES IN MAJOR POLICY SHIFT

"There are concrete agreements regarding Patriot licenses. At our meeting, President Trump stressed that he had made his final decision: Ukraine will receive licenses to produce Patriot missiles,'" Zelenskyy posted Friday.

President Trump had previously hesitated to grant Ukraine the licenses.

Fox News Digital contacted the White House for comment.

item.title: Former UK Prime Minister Tony Blair warns Europe ‘we don’t win’ in war without US support
item.description: Former U.K. Prime Minister Tony Blair insisted British leaders should preserve their alliance with Trump, calling the U.S. "indispensable" to security.
item.content:encoded:
Former U.K. Prime Minister Tony Blair warned that Europe could find itself unable to prevail in a conflict with Russia if it loses the backing of the United States, saying British leaders should preserve their alliance with President Donald Trump.

"If we get drawn into a conflict without the support of America, we don't win," Blair told "Saturday in America" host Kayleigh McEnany.

"This is an essential relationship," he continued. "And the reason why I thought we should have supported President Trump when he asked for the use of our bases is in circumstances where your ally is an indispensable part of your security, and they come asking for help, it’s wise to give it to them."

RUBIO QUESTIONS ‘POINT’ OF NATO AFTER ALLIES BLOCKED US FROM USING BASES DURING IRAN CONFLICT

Blair, who served as Britain’s prime minister from 1997 to 2007, called the U.S.-U.K. relationship "an essential" part of the West’s security as European nations debate the threat Russian President Vladimir Putin could pose to NATO countries.

While Blair personally believes Putin poses no real threat to countries outside of Ukraine, he acknowledged that others across Europe hold a different belief.

US INTEL WARNS RUSSIA COULD LAUNCH LIMITED ATTACK ON NATO ALLY IN EFFORT TO FRAGMENT ORGANIZATION: REPORT

"I might be wrong [about Putin]. And there are a lot of people in Europe who think he's got malicious intent towards NATO countries," he said.

Blair's comments come as some European leaders have raised their voices in concern over Russia, including after one recent instance in which an explosives-laden drone was discovered near a Ukrainian cargo plane at an airport in Germany.

A series of other events — including airspace violations, arson and more — have similarly raised eyebrows and pointed toward escalation, per USA Today.

The U.S. and European nations continue to seek ways to bolster Ukraine's defense and deter Russia while refraining from complete involvement in the conflict.

item.title: Someone could have opened an account in your name. Check now
item.description: New account fraud victims jumped 31% in 2025, reaching 5.4 million. Criminals open accounts you may never see on your regular bank statements.
item.content:encoded:
Most people think identity theft means someone gets into a bank account or starts charging things to a credit card you already use. But there is another kind of identity theft that can be much harder to spot. A criminal can use your name, Social Security number, birthdate or other personal information to open a brand-new account in your name. And this problem is growing fast. Javelin Strategy & Research found that the number of new-account fraud victims jumped 31% in 2025, rising from 4.2 million to 5.4 million. That was the sharpest increase among the fraud types Javelin tracked.

The fraudulent account could be a credit card sent to an address you have never lived at. It could be a phone or utility account with a company you have never used. Someone could even try to open a buy now, pay later account using your identity. That is what makes this kind of fraud so sneaky. The criminal may never touch an account you already monitor, so there may be no suspicious charge staring back at you from your bank statement. You may find out only when a strange bill arrives, a lender checks your credit, a debt collector calls or you spot an account that clearly does not belong to you. The good news is there are ways to look for those clues before the problem gets even bigger.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Get Better Healthcare With AI replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class Get Better Healthcare With AI has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay now at CyberGuyLive.com

6 IN 10 IDENTITY CRIMES NOW BEGIN WITH A NEW ACCOUNT

With fraud on an account you already use, you have a decent chance of spotting it quickly. A strange purchase shows up, your bank sends an alert or your card suddenly stops working. New-account fraud can stay much quieter. A criminal applies for a new account using enough of your personal information to pose as you. If the application goes through, the account may be tied to an address, phone number or email account the criminal controls. As far as the lender or company knows, you opened it. The first clue could be a hard inquiry on your credit report, a new account you do not recognize or mail welcoming you to a service you never signed up for. But there is an important catch. Not every type of account appears on all three credit reports, and some phone, utility or buy now, pay later activity may not appear there. That is why checking your credit reports helps, but it should not be the only thing you watch.

Criminals have more stolen personal information to work with than ever. Years of data breaches have exposed names, Social Security numbers, birthdates, addresses, email addresses and other details that can help someone impersonate you. A criminal may also combine information from multiple breaches, phishing attacks or data broker records to build a much fuller picture of your identity. At the same time, opening financial and other accounts online has become incredibly convenient. You can apply from your couch and sometimes get a decision within minutes. That convenience works in our favor when we are the ones applying. It can also give criminals more opportunities to try stolen identities without ever walking into a bank or store. The Federal Reserve has also warned that digital account openings create new opportunities for fraudsters, especially as stolen personal information and more sophisticated technology become easier for criminals to use.

A criminal may not get everything needed to steal your identity from one breach. Your name and email could come from one leak. An older breach might expose other personal information. A people-search site may help fill in an address or phone number. Put enough pieces together and a criminal may have what they need to start testing your identity against lenders, retailers, phone carriers and other companies. That also helps explain why identity theft can seem to come out of nowhere. The information used against you may have been floating around for months or even years before someone decided to use it.

New-account fraud can leave clues in several places, and some of them are easy to miss if you do not know where to look.

You do not need to wait for a strange bill or collection call to find out something is wrong. A few quick checks can help you spot signs of new-account fraud before it turns into a bigger problem.

Go to AnnualCreditReport.com and review your Equifax, Experian and TransUnion reports. Free reports are currently available weekly, so you can check all three at once or stagger your reviews throughout the year.

Pay close attention to accounts, hard inquiries, addresses and other information you do not recognize. If something looks strange, do not assume it is harmless.

A credit freeze can make it much harder for someone to open a new credit account in your name because lenders generally cannot access your frozen credit report. Freezes are free to place and lift, they do not hurt your credit score and they stay in place until you remove them. You need to contact Equifax, Experian and TransUnion separately to freeze all three files.

Look for messages about accounts you never opened, especially welcome notices, bills, password-reset messages and application updates.

Your bank and credit card companies may offer account alerts at no charge. Identity theft monitoring can go further by watching for certain credit inquiries, new accounts and other signs that someone may be using your information. See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at Cyberguy.com . The faster you know something has changed, the faster you can investigate it.

IS YOUR SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER ON THE DARK WEB?

If you spot an account you do not recognize, act quickly. These six steps can help you shut down the fraud, limit the damage and start cleaning up your records.

Call the company's fraud department. Explain that you did not open the account and ask them to close or freeze it. Keep any confirmation they send you.

Go to IdentityTheft.gov and create an FTC Identity Theft Report and recovery plan. That report can also help when you dispute fraudulent information.

A fraud alert tells businesses to take extra steps to verify your identity before opening new credit. An initial fraud alert is free, lasts one year and requires you to contact only one of the three major credit bureaus. That bureau must notify the other two. A credit freeze goes further by restricting access to your credit report. To freeze all three reports, contact each bureau separately.

Contact any credit bureau showing the fraudulent account and ask it to block the identity-theft information from your report. To use the FTC's blocking process, send the bureau a copy of your FTC Identity Theft Report, proof of your identity and a letter identifying the fraudulent information. You can also dispute inaccurate information directly with the credit bureau.

Your bank and credit card companies may offer account alerts at no charge, so turn those on first. Identity theft monitoring can add another layer by watching for certain credit inquiries, newly opened accounts and other signs that someone may be using your personal information. That can be especially helpful with new-account fraud because the criminal may never touch the accounts you already check. See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at CyberGuy.com.

Write down who you contacted, when you contacted them and what they told you. Save letters, emails, case numbers and copies of anything you submit. Those records can save you a lot of frustration if you need to follow up later.

9 WARNING SIGNS OF IDENTITY THEFT YOU SHOULD NEVER IGNORE

New-account fraud can be especially tough to spot because the criminal may never touch the bank accounts or credit cards you already watch. That is exactly why I want you to check all three of your credit reports instead of waiting for a strange bill or collection call to show up. You can pull your reports for free, look for unfamiliar accounts or inquiries and consider freezing your credit when you are not applying for anything new. Then add alerts or identity monitoring if you want another set of eyes watching for activity you might otherwise miss. The big takeaway here is speed. A fraudulent account that sits unnoticed for months can turn into damaged credit, collections and a much bigger cleanup job. Catch it early and you have a far better chance of shutting it down before things snowball.

When was the last time you checked all three of your credit reports for an account you never opened? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: The wildest things celebrity guest picker Johnny Knoxville said on College Gameday
item.description: Johnny Knoxville compared Lane Kiffin to toe fungus and called Texas the real UTI during a College Gameday guest spot in Knoxville, Tennessee Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
It's been quite the scene in Knoxville, Tennessee, Saturday. President Donald Trump is in attendance, the No. 1 team in the country is in town, Holly Rowe and Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian had their first interview since he abruptly ended their interview following their upset win over Ohio State, and Johnny Knoxville was ESPN College Gameday's celebrity guest picker. While dressed in a complete Tennessee Volunteers football uniform, Knoxville made some statements that were just as outrageous as some of his stunts on MTV’s hit show "Jackass."

LANE KIFFIN COULDN'T HELP HIMSELF, TAKES PETTY SHOT AT OLE MISS FANS AFTER LSU LOSS IN HIS RETURN TO OXFORD

When choosing the winner of the Missouri and Mississippi State, Knoxville hilariously took aim at McAfee's musical career. "I'm so sure about this game, that if Missouri loses, I will punish myself by listening to Pat McAfee's new album on repeat until Halloween." McAfee busted out a huge laugh immediately with Knoxville saying, "No offense."

PAT MCAFEE MIGHT HAVE MADE AN ILLEGAL IMMIGRATION JOKE ON 'COLLEGE GAMEDAY,' LIBERALS LOSE THEIR MINDS

During the Georgia vs Oklahoma selection, Knoxville assigned some pretty gross medical ailments to the respective teams. "You know, I'm from Knoxville so this is like rooting for the gout versus the syphilis. I'm going with the gout. I'll take Georgia," Knoxville stated, while McAfee put his face in his hands and Herbstreit shook his head in disbelief. I hope your kids weren't watching this selection, folks.

LSU head coach Lane Kiffin is the butt of many jokes this season after his rough departure from Ole Miss in the offseason and the loss last Saturday against his former squad so the moment to choose LSU or Texas A&M was primed for Knoxville to lower the boom in his own, special, usually gross way. "I don't know how anyone can root for Lane "Left Out in the Parking Lot" Kiffin. He is to college football what toe fungus is to flip flops. I'm going with A&M."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Now it was time for the Volunteers fans to pick the winner of Texas vs Tennessee. After discussing the Tennessee defensive questions, and taking a shot at Texas' offense, Knoxville made his pick. "After the game today, Tennessee will remain the real UT, and Texas will remain the real UTI." The reaction by Rece Davis and Desmond Howard was priceless. Both of them couldn't believe their ears, but it shouldn't have been a shocker after two-plus minutes of unhinged statements.

SEC CROWD GREETS TRUMP WITH MASSIVE CHEERS AHEAD OF TENNESSEE-TEXAS SHOWDOWN

Knoxville also jokingly tried slipping a referee a $20 bill pregame during an interview. He was truly a one-of-a-kind, PG-13-rated guest.

item.title: Trump's home county hits pause on data centers over environment and electric bill concerns
item.description: Palm Beach County passed a one-year moratorium on data centers amid concerns over environmental impact, noise pollution, and rising electric bills.
item.content:encoded:
Palm Beach County — home to President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago — passed a one-year moratoriam on the planning and construction of data centers as commissioners seek to conduct a thorough review of data centers’ impacts on the environment, noise pollution, and electric bills.

The moratorium, passed on Thursday, comes just weeks after Trump said that communities that reject data centers would "end up being backwards and poor." Among the wealthiest counties in the country, Palm Beach County includes the town of Palm Beach, home to 65 billionaires.

"If you want to go through poverty, crime and squalor, I would say don’t approve of data centers," Trump said from the Oval Office on Sep. 4.

The Palm Beach County Commissioners’ 6-0 vote doesn’t put a permanent ban on data centers. Instead, it gives county leadership time to conduct environmental impact reviews before updating zoning rules for where data centers can be built.

TRUMP’S DATA CENTER PUSH FRACTURES CONGRESS AS LOCAL ANGER EXPLODES: 'GRASPING AT STRAWS'

The moratorium applies to all new applications for data centers with an anticipated peak electrical load of at least 50 megawatts.

"Many communities want the economic benefits a data center brings, but we all fear the higher power bills, the negative environmental impact, disruptive noise, the depletion of water resources," a Palm Beach County resident shared during Thursday’s meeting.

Trump has made expanding data centers and accelerating artificial intelligence a cornerstone of his agenda, arguing that the United States cannot afford to lose the AI race to China and warning that opposition to data centers only benefits Beijing.

Data centers are the physical backbone of artificial intelligence, housing thousands of powerful computers that store and process digital information while providing the computing power needed to train and run AI systems.

Palm Beach County has already approved in 2016 the construction of "Project Tango" — a proposed 202-acre AI data center, which is located 20 miles from Mar-a-Lago. The data center will also be built near an elementary school and homes.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS QUESTION WHETHER AI’S PROMISE OUTWEIGHS ITS RISKS

In July, commissioners voted 6-1 to reject a proposal to expand Project Tango by roughly 1.67 million square feet. But existing approvals for two 100,000-square-foot data center buildings remain in place.

Residents at the Thursday meeting said Project Tango was the driving factor behind the push to hit pause on data center project approvals, with several residents advocating for no data centers to be built.

"I think the best good neighbor data center is no data center," resident Sergei Kelly said. "We have the Everglades to our South and to our West. The coast to our East. I don’t think data centers, especially large data centers they want to build desperately should be here at all."

Fox News Digital reached to the White House and Palm Beach County Commissioners for comment.

item.title: Your favorite grocery and snack items may have disappeared from store shelves in 2026
item.description: Minute Maid frozen juice, Blue Bell Butter Crunch and Cheetos Pizza Puffs are among beloved grocery products reportedly vanishing from shelves in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Shoppers are mourning several grocery store products this year — from a nostalgic juice staple to cult-favorite snack flavors reportedly being cleared from shelves.

Some 2026 grocery exits are confirmed, while others have been reported by food outlets and shoppers.

Coca-Cola confirmed a longtime freezer-aisle exit because of "shifting consumer preferences," The Associated Press (AP) said earlier this year.

DANNON'S DECISION TO KILL BELOVED YOGURT SPARKS FAN REVOLT: 'IT'S WHAT I GOT OUT OF BED FOR'

Meanwhile, PepsiCo announced last year that it planned to reduce nearly 20% of its U.S. product offerings as part of an effort to focus on products with simpler ingredients and functional benefits. 

Food outlets have reported that more than 20 snacks could be affected, though PepsiCo has not confirmed every individual product.

Recently, a list of likely discontinued items across several major brands were featured in Tasting Table. 

OLD-SCHOOL SODA WENT FROM BEING A TOP BRAND TO NEARLY UNFINDABLE

Here are five of the top items.

Coca-Cola is ending Minute Maid frozen orange juice, lemonade and limeade products, which many shoppers remember fondly from childhood. The company said the move ends its presence in the frozen-can category after 80 years.

"My family would buy these to make frozen icees in the summer," one person wrote in the subreddit r/Millennials. "Can't believe they're being discontinued."

"This is devastating. Nothing compares. My comfort drink," another said.

COCA-COLA QUIETLY AXED ONE REAGAN-ERA DRINK THAT DISAPPEARED FROM STORE SHELVES

Blue Bell’s Butter Crunch — vanilla ice cream filled with chunks of crunchy chocolate peanut butter candy — is also gone for now. The company’s own product page says the flavor "is no longer available."

"I want them to bring back Butter Crunch so dang bad," one Reddit user wrote in a thread devoted to Blue Bell flavors shoppers want to see return.

Cheese Pizza Cheetos Puffs returned in 2025 after a 20-year hiatus, but food outlets have reported that the flavor is now being phased out again.

GEN Z TURNS ON CLASSIC SNACKS, FORCING MAJOR GROCERY SHAKE-UP: 'THEY DON'T TRUST THEM'

The pizza-inspired puffs were among the PepsiCo cuts, Allrecipes reported.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

The flavor drew mixed reviews, with some Reddit users saying it did not taste much like pizza, while another said, "I am addicted to these things."

Lay’s Sweet Potato Poppables are another snack reportedly being removed from shelves amid PepsiCo’s broader reductions.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The light, sweet potato-flavored snack no longer appears among the flavors on Lay’s current Poppables page. Reports have said the product is one of several Poppables varieties being discontinued, although PepsiCo has not confirmed.

"These were such a comfort food of mine," one Reddit user lamented. 

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Another said his girlfriend's "heart breaks every time she goes to the store because they no longer carry them."

While some retailers may still have inventory of Smartfood's Movie Theater Butter Popcorn flavor, fans say the flavor has become harder to find following PepsiCo's cuts.

"Smartfood betrayed me and discontinued their Movie Theater Butter flavor, and I'm a wreck," one Reddit user wrote.

item.title: Cruz says winning AI race against China is 'single most important economic question' for America
item.description: Ted Cruz claims China and "effective altruism" backers are waging a deliberate influence campaign to shape AI policy and data center debates.
item.content:encoded:
America's AI race against China, which has become a major point of debate as midterms approach, is a race filled with "coordinated" propaganda, warned Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas.

In recent months, data centers and AI policy have been debated in Congress and at the kitchen tables of American families. But Cruz, who chairs the Senate Commerce Committee, told Fox News Digital that much of the new opposition to data centers is being manipulated by a well-funded and coordinated campaign.

"It's the same reason we saw Middle Eastern countries paying for anti-fracking movements," Cruz said. "Because if they can convince America, 'Don't develop your oil and gas, just buy it from us,' well, that's great for them and terrible for us. The same is true on data centers. If they can convince Americans, 'You don't want data centers here, you want to just rely on the Chinese for AI,' that's great for China, and it's terrible for America."

CHINA EXPERT WARNS BEIJING WANTS AMERICANS — NOT THE CCP — TO SPREAD ITS MESSAGE

Direct funding from the Chinese government into the U.S. on data center policies has not been revealed. However, in June, OpenAI announced it had banned ChatGPT accounts believed to have originated in China, and said that the accounts were generating social media comments and images alleging that data centers are raising electricity costs for Americans.

OpenAI said in a statement that it shut down "two clusters of ChatGPT accounts likely originating from China that [OpenAI] banned after they used our models in support of apparent covert influence operations that promoted narratives in an attempt to manipulate a legitimate debate about American AI and wider tech policies."

Cruz called the effort to craft policy to ensure the U.S. wins the AI race is "the single most important economic question facing America today."

INSIDE THE FAR-LEFT'S ANTI-DATA CENTER PUSH AND WHAT EXPERTS SAY IS DRIVING IT: 'PLAYBOOK WE'VE SEEN BEFORE'

"If China wins, AI will be focused on espionage and propaganda and control and surveillance, because that's the Chinese Communist Party," Cruz said. "It will be their values. They will use AI to try to control you. If America wins, I want American values to be reflected in AI. I want free speech and individualism and free enterprise and privacy to be reflected in AI, not control and power."

Cruz called opposition to AI advancement and data centers the "dominant position on the Democratic side." The third-term Republican said the Democrats' position is aligned with that of big industry players including Anthropic that he said want exemption from antitrust laws and to "get in bed with government" to control AI development.

THE HIDDEN LEFT-WING NETWORK POWERING A ‘CONSERVATIVE’ REBELLION AGAINST A MAJOR TRUMP PRIORITY

Cruz associated this position with leftist ideology and the emerging tech philosophy known as "effective altruism."

"These folks from effective altruism are all hardcore leftists, and they want to use AI to push their leftist ideology," Cruz said. "Part of what we're seeing is a money grab, where there's an old concept in economics called rent seeking, which is big companies typically go to government and say, 'Give me a benefit, entrench me.' We’re seeing the giant AI companies going to government saying, 'Hey, why don't you put us in charge of government and let's set the rules so no one could compete with us.'"

Parker Thayer, an investigative researcher at Capital Research Center in Washington, D.C., told Fox News Digital last week that effective altruism is associated with what he called the "AI doomerism movement."

Facebook co-founder and billionaire Democratic mega-donor Dustin Moskovitz and his wife Cari Tuna have been leading financial backers of organizations associated with the effective altruism movement. Moskovitz left Facebook in 2008.

The couple founded Coefficient Giving, formerly known as Open Philanthropy, and remains its "main funders," according to the organization. Tuna serves as its president.

Coefficient Giving says its artificial intelligence work has expanded rapidly, with $168 million committed to AI safety, security and field-building in 2024 and $351 million in 2025. The organization says it is on track to commit more than $1 billion to AI policy advocacy in 2026.

In a 2021 grant application description, the organization said it seeks "to fund programs and events in a variety of areas of interest to Coefficient Giving — including effective altruism, global catastrophic risks, biosecurity, AI for epistemics, forecasting, and other areas."

In 2015, Coefficient Giving launched "Project Tailwind," an initiative where the Moskovitz-funded organization issued a "call for founders to launch ambitious AI safety initiatives."

item.title: Texas' Steve Sarkisan's first interview with Holly Rowe goes off without a hitch after viral postgame incident
item.description: Steve Sarkisian and Holly Rowe shared a smooth pregame interview at Neyland Stadium before No. 1 Texas faced No. 14 Tennessee on Saturday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
Holly Rowe and Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian’s interview on Saturday was much different from their last one.

After Texas’ thrilling 24-23 comeback win, Sarkisian ran away from Rowe as she attempted to interview him, leaving the ESPN reporter visibly dismayed. On Saturday, prior to the highly anticipated matchup between No. 1 Texas and No. 14 Tennessee at Neyland Stadium, Rowe interviewed Sarkisian right before kickoff, and it went off without a hitch.

Rowe referenced Arch Manning’s Hall of Fame uncle, Peyton Manning, and how members of the Manning family have played well at Neyland Stadium before asking Sarkisian how he had told Arch to make the game his own.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"This is his moment. I want him to go out and have fun with his teammates, right? This team has been great all year. It’s going to continue to play great, but they need to play great together. It’s not about just Arch, it’s about the entire team," Sarkisian told ESPN.

"Thanks so much, coach. Appreciate you," Rowe responded.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Appreciate you," Sarkisian replied as he walked back toward his sideline.

The postgame interview after the Ohio State game went viral, but the attention didn’t stop there. Manning was asked about the viral videos after Texas’ comeback win and pointed to an AI video depicting Sarkisian slapping Rowe, which drew laughs from those in the room.

Manning has since apologized for his comments, and Sarkisian explained that ESPN was dealing with delays and said he wanted to celebrate with his team. The Texas coach said he has a "great relationship" with Rowe that dates back to his playing days at BYU.

Sarkisian hopes he’ll be interviewed by Rowe for a second time on the field after a Longhorns victory on Saturday. At the time of this writing, Texas was up 7-3 on Tennessee in the first quarter.

item.title: Sylvester Stallone shares harrowing new details about abusive childhood
item.description: Sylvester Stallone's upcoming memoir reveals his father's brutal beatings and a mother who never hugged him, shaping the ferocity behind "Rocky" and "Rambo."
item.content:encoded:
Sylvester Stallone isn't looking for pity.

The action star opened up about a childhood marked by abandonment, violence and an almost total absence of affection in a new interview, telling The New York Times that he deliberately left some of the darkest stories out of his book because he didn't want readers to feel sorry for him.

"I didn't put a lot of stuff in the book because I didn't want a pity party … but it was insane," he admitted.

SYLVESTER STALLONE REVEALS WHAT HE SAID TO TRUMP AFTER SURPRISE HOLLYWOOD AMBASSADOR APPOINTMENT

After his parent’s divorce, Stallone spent time living with his father in Maryland. He described his father as volatile and physically abusive.

"The next thing you know — wham! He had very big hands. You just learned to duck a little bit."

One memory particularly stayed with Stallone.

The Hollywood star said his father sent him to a store before church to buy bread. He returned with nut bread after running into friends.

"And he kicked me in the stomach and hit me and like laid me out, got in the car, and went to church."

Stallone said he was left lying in the street, saying, "Really, it's unbelievable. It's unbelievable."

Years later, Stallone confronted his father. When he was in his 40s, Stallone told him, "I wish you and I could be the same age for three minutes." When his father asked him why, he said, "Because I'd like to give you some of your own medicine, and you would know what it'd be like to have your ass kicked."

Stallone said his father then challenged him to fight, explaining, "He was ready to go at 68 years old."

The "Rocky" star connected that fierceness to the one of the characters he's best known for.

"So, when people go, ‘Where do you get the ferocity to play Rambo?' Genetic," he said.

Stallone additionally recalled that his mother never showed affection towards him.

SYLVESTER STALLONE'S 'TULSA KING' SEASON 4 TEASER SPARKS FAN FRENZY: 'THE KING IS BACK!'

"My mother never — and my brother will attest — hugged me. Ever, ever," Stallone shared.

His father rarely showed affection either. But when Stallone was about 9, he said he fell asleep in the car after working around his father's horses. His father placed Stallone's head on his knee and rested his hand on his head.

"And I never got over that," he admitted.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Earlier in the interview, Stallone described being sent to live in a boarding house when he was very young, where his parents visited only once a month.

"I just was raised by strangers, you know, in a boarding house. And it became sort of a natural environment. And my parents were really never nurturing, so this was actually a bonus compared to where I was living."

That emotional deprivation, Stallone acknowledged, shaped the man he became.

When asked whether it made him tough, he replied, "In the wrong way, yeah, it did. It made me very tough."

But the toughness came at a cost. Stallone said he didn't experience what he considers "real, real, real, real true love" until he was around 70, when he experienced it with his wife and kids, saying, "And that's a big pity. It really is."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Stallone went on to build one of Hollywood's most recognizable careers, writing and starring as Rocky Balboa and going on to play John Rambo. The original "Rocky" received 10 Oscar nominations and won three Academy Awards, including best picture.

Off-screen, Stallone has five children from two of his three marriages.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Stallone married his first wife, Sasha Czack, in 1974. They divorced in 1985 and shared two sons, Sage and Seargeoh. Stallone married "Rocky IV" co-star Brigitte Nielsen later in 1985, and the couple divorced in 1987.

Stallone married Jennifer Flavin in 1997. They share three daughters, Sophia, Sistine and Scarlet.

item.title: Rob Gronkowski calls Chargers 'probably the biggest mess in the NFL' right now after rough start
item.description: Rob Gronkowski called the Los Angeles Chargers the biggest mess in the NFL, blasting Justin Herbert's play and the struggling offensive line.
item.content:encoded:
We’re already onto Week 3 in the 2026 NFL season, and teams are beginning to show their identities, proving they could be playoff contenders, or worse, teams that need some serious changes.

And while some squads have been surprises in good fashion, others haven’t.

For future Pro Football Hall of Fame tight end Rob Gronkowski, the Los Angeles Chargers fall into the latter bucket.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"The Los Angeles Chargers I would say are probably the biggest mess in the NFL in terms of how they’re playing and where they should be," he told OutKick in New York City during an event for Bounty.

In the spirit of his partnership, we asked "Gronk" who is biggest mess in the NFL is after the first two weeks. He brought up the Miami Dolphins at first, but he believes it was "expected" considering their roster questions entering the season.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

But nobody expected the Chargers, a team led by head coach Jim Harbaugh with new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, to be 0-2 after facing the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders – two teams that many didn’t predict to have playoff hopes in 2026 – to start the year.

So, Gronkowski was quite candid about what he’s seen thus far in Inglewood, California from that group.

"That’s a mess over there right now," he said. "They gotta just grab a Bounty paper towel and wipe off all their linemen, because they’re not clean. They’re dirty and they’re falling all over the place. Get the blocks down schematically and keep Justin Herbert clean in the pocket so he can perform."

The Chargers were expected to be a team to watch for the Super Bowl this season, especially with McDaniel coming in with his explosive offensive scheme. But the Chargers have produced just 14 points per game across their two contests, which is the third-lowest average in the league thus far. They are also 23rd in total offensive yards averaged per game, and the tape shows why.

Herbert is having a rough time finding any rhythm on offense, and while the offensive line, a pain point for the Chargers in recent seasons, has a lot to do with it, he’s also not making the plays many expect him to thus far. Herbert has thrown just two touchdowns, while being picked off three times in two games. He’s also completed just 59.3% of his passes.

However, Gronkowski implored that one player, even if it is your quarterback, can’t take sole blame for a team not hitting the mark everyone expected them to.

"It’s not just one thing that’s going wrong. It’s a lot of things going wrong," Gronkowski said. "The quarterback just not playing good ball, the offensive coordinator just not reading his team and not putting them in the right position. Offensive line is stinking it [up]. The wide receivers just not making the plays when they need to. It’s a collective of everything. Like, it’s in the air – it’s not just one thing.

"So, you have to fix everything as a whole when you go down that low. …It’s football. It’s such a team game that one player can’t make you collapse the way they’re collapsing. It’s everyone as a whole."

It’s still just two games into the season, but the Chargers have a gauntlet of a schedule moving forward. They will head to Buffalo this week to face the 2-0 Bills, while having to take on the Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos, Kansas City Chiefs, Los Angeles Rams, Houston Texans and Baltimore Ravens after that.

item.title: Legal expert details what travelers are entitled to after massive East Coast flight cancellations
item.description: Under U.S. law, travelers affected by the severed cable flight disruptions can claim a full cash refund, but rebooking first could void that right.
item.content:encoded:
After a severed fiber optic cable disrupted thousands of flights to and from East Coast airports on Monday, customers are entitled to a full refund under U.S. law, but they also have other options, Eric Napoli, the chief legal officer at AirHelp, told Fox News Digital.

"Under U.S. domestic law on flights, the rules are that you're entitled to a full cash refund," Napoli explained.

"If you are flying to and from Europe and fall under European rules, if the cause of the delay is directly attributable to the airline, then you could be entitled to up to $700. In this case, this is completely outside of the airline's control. This is a tower-to-ground issue, so you don't get any compensation. But what you are entitled to is — if you decide not to take that flight, or whatever flight they give you next — a full cash refund," Napoli said.

U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed Amtrak for the cancellations, claiming that a construction crew cut the cable. However, the company quickly pushed back.

LAGUARDIA AIRPORT RUNWAY SHUT DOWN AFTER SINKHOLE DISCOVERED DURING ROUTINE MORNING INSPECTION

"This incident occurred on New Jersey Transit property and involved a New Jersey Transit contractor," Amtrak said in a statement.

NJ Transit acknowledged working on the site where the cable was cut, but claimed "the crew was digging approximately 10 feet away from the utility markings."

Because the incident was not caused by any of the airlines, customers traveling to and from Europe are not entitled to a $700 cash payment that European law would entitle them to if the airport caused the delays, Napoli said.

DELTA FLIGHT DIVERTED TWICE AFTER LAVATORY LEAK FLOODS CABIN, LEAVES PASSENGERS STRANDED FOR HOURS

"In this scenario, European law wouldn't say that the airline has to pay compensation because the network connectivity issue was completely outside of the airline's control — as it would be, for example, if a hurricane were flying in. If the aircraft had a technical issue and they weren't able to fix it in time, that's part of the airline's business and operating model, so an airline would have to pay up to $700," he told Fox News Digital.

Customers are entitled to a full cash refund under U.S. law. However, if they take an offer from the airlines to rebook their flights, they lose the option to get a refund, Napoli said.

"Generally what happens is the airline will come to the passenger and say, 'Either we've canceled the flight or we've rescheduled the flight for the next day, and we've put you on another flight.' The passenger then has the option to say, 'Do I want to take the other flight, or do I not want to?' Maybe now there's no reason to go see the game in Philadelphia, so you don't want to be rescheduled. In that case, you get your money back. If you decide to take the flight, then you wouldn't get your money back because you have consumed a service," he explained.

He recommended customers take initiative in receiving their refunds rather than waiting for the airlines to reimburse them.

"Generally, if you don't ask for it, you're not going to get it, so you have to be pretty proactive. Airlines have gotten really good now with offering rescheduled flights in their apps, because a situation like this is also a headache for them. The airlines have to suddenly find all of these people and rebook them. It's Tetris — along with the domino effect of delay after delay. The airlines will try to help, but for other things like getting a food voucher, a taxi, or a hotel, the traveler is going to have to be savvy and proactive," he continued.

"That's where AirHelp comes in and helps. We have lots of information on our website and a 24/7 chat that keeps you updated. We also have an app that can let you know if your flight is delayed or if incoming flights are on time, so you can look at sources like us. When it comes to things like compensation under European laws, airlines don't make it easy for you," Napoli added.

Napoli ultimately counseled travelers to remain savvy and calm.

"Having information beforehand and knowing how to navigate is always best. Be prepared. Things can go wrong, and we get angry and upset. But getting angry at the people at the airport desk doesn't help the situation — it just makes you angrier. It's best to keep calm, talk to people civilly, and hopefully, things will work out," he told Fox News Digital.

Fox News Digital contacted the Department of Transportation, Amtrak and New Jersey Transit for comment.

item.title: SEC crowd greets Trump with massive cheers ahead of Tennessee-Texas showdown
item.description: Trump arrived in Knoxville to a roaring Neyland Stadium crowd as the new-look Air Force One flew over ahead of the No. 14 Vols vs. No. 1 Texas kickoff.
item.content:encoded:
Donald Trump has arrived in Tennessee for the biggest college football game of the day, and — to the surprise of approximately nobody — the Neyland Stadium crowd went nuts as Air Force I flew over the stadium.

The president arrived in Knoxville about 40 minutes before kickoff of today's marquee showdown between the Vols and No. 1 Texas. It's the first meeting between the two schools since the Cotton Bowl in 1969. Tennessee comes in ranked 14th in the country, while the Longhorns are No. 1 and two weeks removed from an upset of Ohio State.

That was in Austin, though. Today's game is in Knoxville, with the eyes of everyone — including the president — on them.

TRUMP TO ATTEND TEXAS VS TENNESSEE IN HIGH-STAKES COLLEGE FOOTBALL SHOWDOWN

Obviously, it's a very pro-Trump crowd for today's ... SEC ... showdown. Who would've thunk it?! Forget the approval ratings. If Trump goes to an SEC game, he's gonna be cheered. Heavily.

Oddly enough, the only place he may have been met with some boos would've been Austin. Look at what the College GameDay crowd did to Ted Cruz two weeks ago.

TENNESSEE FANS EXCITED FOR TRUMP'S ATTENDANCE AT GAME VS TEXAS: 'I HOPE HE STAYS THE WHOLE GAME'

It was brutal.

But Knoxville is different. Tennessee is a different animal. Fans were told to get to the stadium hours before today's noon kickoff due to heightened security, and they listened.

OutKick's Trey Wallace reports seats were nearly full at the time Trump arrived, which also shouldn't surprise anyone given the school ran a nifty little promotion to entice the masses ...

All drinks, including beer, which half-price between 9 a.m and 10 a.m. That's right. You read that right. Half-price beer at 9 a.m., for a college football game at noon? What could go wrong!

Seems like everyone listened. And for those who did, they were treated to quite the show from Air Force I.

item.title: Bill Maher credits Trump’s ‘kick a--’ crime approach as violent offenses fall across America
item.description: Bill Maher praised Donald Trump's tough-on-crime persona on "Real Time," saying the "f---around-and-find-out president" sent a message to bad guys.
item.content:encoded:
Comedian Bill Maher offered surprising praise for President Donald Trump's handling of crime Friday, telling his audience that the president's tough-guy persona may have played a role in a nationwide drop in violent crime.

"It's not just drug crime that's way down, it's all crime," Maher said during Friday’s episode of HBO’s "Real Time," adding, "And again, probably much of it is not political. It's because you can't move two inches in America without being tracked, photographed, and followed by a Flock camera."

According to the late-night host, the president is a "bad a--" and it's childish to pretend" his tough on crime stance isn't having an impact. 

Maher went on to credit both Democratic policies and Trump with contributing to lower nationwide crime rates.

MAHER MOCKS LIBERALS FOR STILL PANICKING ABOUT TRUMP'S ANTICS, PERSONALITY AFTER 10 YEARS

"It's also because when Democrats expand the safety net, there are less desperate people," Maher said. "And because Trump is a bad a--."

Maher added that while he does not "agree with many of [Trump’s] methods," he cannot argue that the president’s tough-on-crime approach has yielded successful results.

TRUMP TO RALLY WITH NEW YORK POLICE IN HIGHLIGHTING HISTORIC COAST-TO-COAST VIOLENT CRIME DROP

"Is doing it this way the right thing? No. But it's just childish to pretend that when you elect a f---around-and-find-out president, a no-more-Mr.-Nice-Guy, boot-in-your-a--, ‘V for Vendetta,’ kick-a-- and take names, say-hello-to-my-little-friend president, that's not going to have some effect on crime," he continued.

"He has UFC fights on the lawn," Maher concluded. "I think the bad guys got the message."

KASH PATEL TO TOUT 'LARGEST' YEAR-TO-YEAR VIOLENT CRIME DROP IN US HISTORY

According to the FBI’s Crime Data Explorer, reported violent crime nationwide fell 9% from June 2025 through May 2026. Robbery saw the steepest drop, at 19.4%, followed by murder at 18.7%, rape at 10% and aggravated assault at 6.2%.

Retired FBI Supervisory Special Agent Jason Pack also pointed to the potential for bipartisan agreement on crime, telling Fox News Digital that "people may have strong disagreements with other parts of an agenda," but that "there can still be common ground around getting violent offenders off the street and making neighborhoods safer."

CRIME IS FALLING, OFFICIALS SAY — VICTIMS CLAIM REPORTING ISN’T WORTH IT

"You don’t have to wear somebody’s campaign button to admit when something appears to be working. That’s probably why you’re hearing even some of the president’s critics acknowledge what they’re seeing on crime," Pack said.

He emphasized the need for collaboration among local, state and federal law enforcement to make a meaningful difference in fighting crime across the country.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"People can and do disagree about politics. That’s nothing new. But most folks want the same things when they get home at the end of the day," Pack said, adding, "We may never get all the way back to the days when people left the front door unlocked, but folks ought to be able to feel secure in their own neighborhood and know violent offenders are being taken off the street. That’s not red or blue. It seems to me that’s red, white and blue."

The White House also praised the decline in crime, pointing to the statistics in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"President Trump promised to make America safe again and the data proves he has done just that. He has delivered the largest decrease in violent crime in American history," a White House spokesperson said. "Unlike Defund-the-Police Democrats, President Trump will always stand with our law enforcement officers and deliver safer American neighborhoods."

item.title: US, China strike deal to lower tariffs on $30B in goods after Trump-Xi Washington summit
item.description: The United States and China agreed to slash tariffs on $30 billion in goods after Trump and Xi Jinping's three-day Washington summit this week.
item.content:encoded:
The United States and China agreed to lower tariffs on $30 billion worth of goods traded between the two countries following a three-day summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, D.C.

According to the White House, the $30 billion in reciprocal tariff reductions apply to "non-sensitive goods."

U.S. exports including agricultural products, fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices will receive favorable tariff treatment in China. Meanwhile, U.S. imports of Chinese-made small appliances, toys, holiday decorations and children's car seats will also receive preferential treatment.

The agreement was reached through the U.S.-China Board of Trade, a body first proposed during Trump's visit to China in May and formally established during Xi's visit to Washington this week.

XI PRAISES US STATE VISIT 'PERFECTION' AS TRUMP CALLS MEETINGS 'VERY PRODUCTIVE'

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC on Friday that "a lot more details" about the new trade agreement will be released on Monday.

Greer said the tariff terms were hammered out after weeks of negotiations. Neither country has released the final tariff rates or all the products that will receive favored status going forward.

This marks one of the most significant cooldowns in the trade war Trump launched against China in February 2025, when he levied a 10% tariff on all Chinese imports, citing Beijing's alleged role in the fentanyl crisis and illegal immigration. China hit back with levies on U.S. coal, liquefied natural gas, crude oil and cars.

BESSENT REVEALS EXTENSION TO BUSAN AGREEMENT WITH CHINA UNTIL JANUARY

At their peak, U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods reached a staggering 145% in April 2025, shortly after Trump unveiled his "Liberation Day" reciprocal tariffs. China responded with tariffs of up to 125% on U.S. goods.

U.S. and Chinese negotiators met in Geneva in May 2025 and agreed to a 90-day truce that lowered U.S. tariffs to 30% and China's to 10%. The agreement was extended for another 90 days in August.

Trump and Xi reached another tentative agreement during talks in South Korea in October 2025. Under the deal, China agreed to crack down on fentanyl precursors, resume purchases of U.S. soybeans and ease restrictions on rare-earth exports, while the United States agreed to further ease tariffs.

The two countries will now use the Board of Trade to negotiate additional tariff reductions and other trade disputes, leaving open the possibility of broader agreements in the months ahead.

item.title: Craig Carton calls out Pablo Torre for tying Tim Tebow to alleged Life Surge scam: 'Shame on you'
item.description: Craig Carton slammed Pablo Torre for dragging Tim Tebow into his Life Surge investigative report, saying the report could be actionable defamation.
item.content:encoded:
Craig Carton called out investigative reporter Pablo Torre for his focus on Tim Tebow in a recent report on Life Surge.

Torre alleged that the Christian-focused organization used Tebow as part of a predatory business model that pressured people to hand over thousands of dollars for advice without seeing a return on their investment.

Carton called Torre a "brilliant investigative reporter" but criticized him for linking Tebow to the organization’s alleged conduct without establishing that Tebow knew about it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"Tim Tebow doesn't deserve to be dragged into this unless you got him nailed. And if you don't have him nailed to the cross on this story, you have defamed him. And if I'm Tim Tebow, I find that to be actionable. I find that to be regrettable," Carton said on a recent episode of OutKick’s "The Craig Carton Show."

Tebow has since come out and said he is "pausing" his relationship with Life Surge.

"I think the allegations are extremely, extremely serious, and it’s something that we take very serious," Tebow told The Gainesville Sun. "And so, for us, we’re having our team do an investigation, but also pausing our relationship until we can learn more about the facts to be able to understand more."

Mother Jones, which collaborated with Torre on the investigation, reported that Tebow spoke at 20 Life Surge events between 2024 and 2025 and was slated to speak at about as many events in 2026. Carton took no issue with Torre’s investigation but lambasted Torre for what the longtime radio host characterized as using Tebow’s name to further his own career.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"You’re using Tim Tebow’s name and popularity to further your own career. You’re using Tim Tebow to get attention for your story. Whether that story is accurate or not, I’ll take the leap of faith that you’ve reported as an allegation about this Life Surge company that it might even be accurate and factual, and we need to get involved. We need to get district attorneys involved and do a thorough, real investigation to see if they’re committing some type of predatory fraud against honest, God-fearing, blue-collar people who might be losing their life savings under the guise of religion," Carton said.

"That would be awful if that's happening. But how dare you sully the name and reputation of a man who has only done things for others? A man that has dedicated his life to service of his Lord."

Carton criticized Torre for putting Tebow in a bad spot when his reporting did not establish that the Florida Gators legend knew about or participated in the alleged conduct. Carton argued that the report forced Tebow to put out a statement and damaged his public reputation.

"When you go down that road and you sully the reputation of somebody who's dedicated his entire life to service, that is a slippery slope that I want no part of," Carton said.

"So, you better have this locked down, Pablo, and maybe you do, but to throw out an allegation, attach a dude's name to it? Shame on you."

item.title: Scientists reveal surprisingly easy exercise that may boost your mood in just 10 minutes
item.description: A University of Tsukuba study found that a slow 10-minute jog boosted attention, self-control and mood in young adults by activating the prefrontal cortex.
item.content:encoded:
It might not take an all-out sprint or long trail run to lift your mood and sharpen focus, according to a new study.

A new study from the University of Tsukuba in Japan looked at 24 healthy young adults who completed a slow, 10-minute run on the treadmill in one session and rested in another.

After the easy jog, participants performed faster on a test of attention and self-control and reported feeling more alert and pleasant than they did after the resting phase, according to the small study, published in the journal Imaging Neuroscience in August.

'PERFECT' WORKOUT FORMULA CAN TAKE JUST 10 MINUTES A DAY, HILARIA BALDWIN SAYS

Brain monitoring after the jog also showed more activity in parts of the prefrontal cortex, the area of the brain responsible for focus and decision-making.

The jog was purposely kept easy, with participants going at speeds from 1.9 to 3.7 mph on the treadmill. Their average heart rates clocked in at 105 to 107 beats per minute.

"A single bout of running, even at very slow speed, elicits a pleasant mood and improved executive function," the researchers found.

SIMPLE BODY MOVEMENT COULD HELP THE BRAIN 'CLEAN ITSELF,' RESEARCHERS FIND

The finding "sheds light on the slow running benefits to brain health," they added. 

The benefits, they noted, stuck around even after participants' heart rates returned to baseline.

JUST 10 MINUTES OF DAILY FLOOR EXERCISES MAY IMPROVE BALANCE AND AGILITY, STUDY FINDS

The greater the up-and-down head movement during the jog, the more positive the participants' mood was afterward, though that finding was exploratory and does not necessarily prove cause and effect.

5 COMMON WALKING MISTAKES THAT COULD HURT YOUR PROGRESS, ACCORDING TO AN EXPERT

"Easy movement triggers the norepinephrine and dopamine pathways that wake up the part of the brain that is in charge of focus and self-control," said Dr. John La Puma, a California-based internist and author of "Indoor Epidemic," who was not involved in the study.

Experts agree, however, that it does not mean one brief workout could be a cure-all.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"A brief jog should help someone get some energy in their system, which may make them feel better about themselves mentally and help them focus," said Dr. Scott Nass, a California-based family medicine physician at SwiftCareMD.

But Nass, who also wasn't involved in the research, said that the effect is likely temporary.

For people living with depression or anxiety, a jog may briefly clear the mind but is "no substitute for medical care," he told Fox News Digital.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The study was also limited in that it included just 24 healthy, young adults and measured outcomes immediately after just one exercise session. 

The findings cannot be assumed to apply to older adults, novice runners or people with health conditions and larger studies are needed to confirm the results, Nass said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

For a practical approach, La Puma suggested taking a 10-minute walk outside before the most mentally demanding part of the day. 

Add 30-second jogging intervals, keeping the pace easy enough to speak in full sentences without becoming breathless, he said.

People with heart disease, high blood pressure, Type 1 diabetes, recent surgery or joint pain should check with a clinician before starting a new routine, La Puma advised.

Fox News Digital reached out to the researchers for comment.

item.title: 'Mike & Molly' star Billy Gardell admits weight loss surgery 'probably saved' his life
item.description: Billy Gardell says bariatric surgery "probably saved my life" after type 2 diabetes and heart concerns forced him to make a drastic decision.
item.content:encoded:
"Mike & Molly" star Billy Gardell is sharing how his dramatic weight loss following his bariatric surgery in 2021 has changed his life.

During a recent appearance on the "Breaking Bread" podcast, the 57-year-old actor said his decision to undergo the surgery "probably saved my life" and described the circumstances which led to him deciding that was the right route for him.

He explained that he had developed type 2 diabetes, as well as "some cholesterol stuff, some heart stuff," joking that his doctor told him that "after 50 the warranties start running out."

"You can't outrun those. I think the only reason I was able to survive as long as I did is one, I got decent genetics, and two was I played some sports when I was younger. So I was a big fat guy, but I was a pretty solid fat guy, and I could carry the weight for a long time, but eventually you can't outrun that."

'REMEMBER THE TITANS' STAR ETHAN SUPLEE SAYS ONE HARD TRUTH FUELED HIS 300-POUND WEIGHT LOSS

After a certain point, Gardell said his doctor approached him and said, "You have to do something."

"I got to the point where I hurt my knee and I couldn't even walk for exercise, and I was like, I have to do something drastic," he said. "So I got the surgery, and it's been a couple years now and I probably saved my life. I'm not on any medication. Diabetes is gone."

Five years after the surgery, the actor explained he has "to be real selective" about what he eats, because he only has "12 ounces to work with," but said the issue with that is "the fat Hulk is still running around" in his mind wanting to overindulge.

Aside from saving his life, the surgery and resulting weight loss also allowed him to do things he couldn't do before, including hiking with his wife and buying something "off the rack" when shopping at the mall.

"It's just those little freedoms that you go, 'Wow, man. I'm so grateful I can do this now,'" he said. "I know those are simple, stupid things, but they mean the world to me."

Gardell explained he decided to get healthy not only for himself, but also for his wife, Patty Knight and their son, William, calling them "my motivating factors."

"It was like I don't want to survive what I've survived, succeed where I succeeded, and then not be able to get out of a chair. So I had to look that in its face. And for anybody out there struggling, if I can do it, you can do it. And don't let nobody tell you different. Do whatever it takes."

Throughout his life, Gardell said he would often fluctuate, losing and gaining 30 pounds every year, noting at his heaviest, he weighed 379 pounds.

During an interview with People in December 2025, the actor said he now maintains his weight through diet and exercise, noting, "I fluctuate between 210 and 215" pounds.

Gardell rose to fame on the hit sitcom "Mike & Molly," playing Melissa McCarthy's husband on the show for six seasons from 2010 to 2016.

item.title: Oxford mayor warns kratom is 'rolling the dice on death' as fears linger over Ole Miss deaths
item.description: Oxford Mayor Robyn Tannehill warns kratom is "rolling the dice on death" after two Ole Miss student deaths rattled the Mississippi campus.
item.content:encoded:
Oxford, Mississippi, Mayor Robyn Tannehill issued a stark warning Saturday about the dangers of kratom and other "gas station drugs" after packaged kratom was recovered during investigations into the deaths of two Ole Miss students.

"To take kratom is really rolling the dice on death..." Tannehill told "Fox & Friends Weekend."

"So our challenge right now is to make our young people understand the dangers of these drugs."

TWO OLE MISS STUDENTS FOUND DEAD AS PACKAGED KRATOM IS RECOVERED AT TWO SITES: OFFICIALS

Tannehill said Oxford's city board passed a law prohibiting the sale of kratom at gas stations seven years ago, and that local authorities have been aware of the substance's dangers for some time.

"This is a substance that our police chief identified as dangerous in 2019, and we immediately took action," she said.

"So these investigations are ongoing. We are always trying to find the bad actors in our community that are choosing to sell these things to kids."

The two students were found dead Monday, Sept. 21, in separate locations — one on campus and the other off campus. Although their causes of death remain undetermined, narcotics detectives are involved in both investigations.

Authorities say, if the reports find fentanyl, a special Mississippi law can be used to target the seller.

THE FRAT OMERTÀ: WHISTLEBLOWER WARNS OF ‘CODE OF SILENCE’ AFTER OLE MISS DEATHS, ALLEGED PENN STATE COKE RING

The news has triggered fears among many Ole Miss students. One student, speaking on "The Faulkner Focus" Thursday, said some students are cautious of what they eat or drink as fears mount on campus.

Tannehill, however, attempted to assuage some of those fears.

"Oxford is an extremely safe town," she said.

"It's a place that, when you walk down the street, people still speak to you," she added. "It's a place that takes care of each other... the issues that we're dealing with right now are the issues that every college campus across the nation is dealing with. It's not unique to Oxford. Unfortunately, the spotlight is on Oxford now because of these two tragic deaths and, if that spotlight can help us save other kids, then my prayer is that this makes somebody check up and say, 'You know what, I'm not going to do that [try any substances].'"

Tannehill also reiterated that the Oxford community is awaiting autopsy and toxicology reports and until those tests are in, many details are speculation. Reports are expected to be completed as early as next week, according to the state's commissioner of public safety.

Oxford police have separately announced arrests in connection with a raid on a tobacco shop accused of trafficking narcotics.

Authorities have identified 18-year-old Aidan Hamilton and 20-year-old Robert Strang as the victims.

Fox News' Adam Sabes, Michael Ruiz and Madison Scarpino contributed to this report.
